total:
\(\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(f\circ g)\not\asymp\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(f)\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(g)\) total No bound exists #

Upper bounds — holds for every total

  • \(\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(f\circ g)=O(\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(f)\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(g))\)
    PednekarPodder26STOC
    Execute the exact inner algorithm for each query of the outer algorithm.

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(f_k\circ\mathrm{OR}_{m_k})}{\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(f_k)\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(\mathrm{OR}_{m_k})}\longrightarrow0\)
    PednekarPodder26composition PednekarPodder26STOC
    Theorem 33 of the STOC submission: total functions; a polynomial saving relative to the product. The outer f_k is the k-fold composition of the four-bit function used in the exact-query/degree separation; the inner function is OR.

Exact quantum query complexity fails to compose within constant factors even for total functions. This does not change the exact composition of deterministic query complexity comp-D or polynomial degree comp-deg, or constant-factor composition of bounded-error quantum queries comp-Q.

see also: \(\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(f)\), \(\mathrm{OR}_n\), comp-Q, comp-deg, \(\mathrm{NE}^d\) data/relations/04-composition.yaml

facts: $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(\mathrm{PARITY}_n) = \lceil n/2\rceil$: the only known factor-2 speedup style behaviour for total functions.
First superlinear-advantage total function: $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(f) = O(\mathrm{D}(f)^{0.8675\ldots})$ [Ambainis13], giving the $1.15$ exponents in the $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}$ column.
It is open whether $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(f) = O(\deg(f))$ for total $f$ [BdW02, Open problem 4].

Exact quantum query complexity does not compose within constant factors on total functions: $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(f_k\circ\mathrm{OR}_{m_k})=o(\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(f_k)\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{E}}(\mathrm{OR}_{m_k}))$ [PednekarPodder26composition, PednekarPodder26STOC]. See comp-QE.

A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing

constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.
